audits.title: 859 Improving Accuracy of Admission Notes Over A Four-Year Period Within an Orthopaedic Trauma Ward: A Four-Cycle Audit
audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons standards for documentation
audits.setting: Orthopaedic trauma ward, Royal Infirmary of Edinburgh

cycle1.result: Initially only two criteria had above 95% compliance; 'note signed' 60%, 'date stamp' 66%, 'contact number' 0%.

audits.intervention: Educational posters; change from handwritten to online admission forms; optimisation of the online proforma with further education.

cycle2.period: Fourth cycle, one year after the third
cycle2.result: All criteria documented in over 95% after further education and proforma modification.

audits.other_findings: Four cycles: posters improved 'note signed' (60% to 96%); moving online improved 'date stamp' (66% to 100%) and 'contact number' (0% to 34%) but reduced 'time recorded' (18% to 0%) and 'name and grade' (74% to 26%).
audits.citation: McCann C, Mackenzie S, White T. 859 Improving Accuracy of Admission Notes Over A Four-Year Period Within an Orthopaedic Trauma Ward: A Four-Cycle Audit. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab134.495.

audits.title: Use of a Pediatric Admission Booklet Significantly Improves the Comprehensiveness of Admission Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: 17 admission documentation standards based on Royal College of Physicians clerking standards and RCPCH/PRSB digital record standards; aim to raise average compliance from 59% to above 90%
audits.setting: Bristol Royal Hospital for Children; tertiary paediatric hospital (paediatric medicine, surgery and orthopaedics)

cycle1.result: Blank continuation sheets: 5 of 17 standards >90%, none 100%; medications 48%, allergies 47%, social history 36%, responsible consultant 8%, accompanying adult 24%, observations 38%.

audits.intervention: Specialty-specific colour-coded pre-printed admission booklets with prompts and tick boxes (medicine, surgery, orthopaedics), introduced March 2019 with teaching at junior doctor handovers.

cycle2.period: From March 2019 (first 40 booklet admissions per specialty)
cycle2.result: Average 33% absolute improvement (P < 0.01); 12 of 17 standards >90% and 4 at 100%; medications 99%, allergies 93%, consultant 88%, accompanying adult 68%, observations 52%.

audits.other_findings: Observations (52%) and investigations (70%) remained poorly documented. Examination findings and plans were already well documented and changed little.
audits.citation: Beverstock A, Lewis C, Bruce D, Barnes J, Kelly A. Use of a Pediatric Admission Booklet Significantly Improves the Comprehensiveness of Admission Documentation: A Quality Improvement Project. Pediatr Qual Saf. 2020;5(1):e247. doi:10.1097/pq9.0000000000000247. PMID: 32190793.

audits.title: Improving Acute Orthopaedic Admission Note Documentation Standards at a Tertiary Centre Through Proforma Introduction: A Quality Improvement Initiative.
audits.standard: Irish HSE Standards and Recommended Practices for Healthcare Records Management and HSE National Model of Care for Trauma and Orthopaedic Surgery documentation standards (checklist)
audits.setting: Regional trauma and tertiary referral centre, Galway University Hospitals; acute orthopaedic trauma admissions

cycle1.result: Unscripted notes: consultant on call 78% (39/50); time of injury 72% (36/50); associated injury 48% (24/50); smoking status 86% (43/50); alcohol 42% (21/50); vital signs 28% (14/50); other systems 14% (7/50).

audits.intervention: Standardised admission proforma developed with multidisciplinary stakeholders after results were presented at departmental teaching, with an accompanying education session; one-month introduction period.

cycle2.result: Proforma notes: consultant on call 100% (p=0.0005); time of injury 100% (p=0.0001); associated injury 100% (p=0.0001); smoking 100% (p=0.0001); alcohol 94% (p=0.0001); vital signs 70% (p=0.0001); other systems 74% (p=0.0001).

audits.other_findings: Admitting doctor grade documentation fell from 92% to 82% and vital signs remained incomplete at 70%. A poll of 16 Irish units found admission proforma use in only 18.8%.
audits.citation: O'Driscoll CS, Condell R, O'Sullivan D, Davey M, Kearns S, Murphy CG. Improving Acute Orthopaedic Admission Note Documentation Standards at a Tertiary Centre Through Proforma Introduction: A Quality Improvement Initiative. audits.standard: Royal College of Surgeons of England record-keeping standards (GSP 2014); target 80% or more for all aspects
audits.setting: University Hospital Waterford; regional orthopaedic trauma service

cycle1.result: Poor documentation of 50% of aspects: author name 50%, date 70%, medications 20%, functional status 30%, investigation results 30%, social history 40%, systemic review 75%

audits.title: An audit on admission clerkings across Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust (LSCFT)
audits.standard: 20-item list of expected clerking components based on trust guidelines
audits.setting: Chorley Mental Health Inpatient Unit, Lancashire and South Cumbria NHS Foundation Trust (psychiatric inpatient wards)

cycle1.result: Highest completion: clerking within 6 hours, consultant face-to-face review within a week and current medication documentation. Lowest completion: clinical impression, bloods within 24 hours, capacity assessment and smoking/substance history (no percentages given).

audits.intervention: Planned: standardised capacity assessment documentation and a clerking checklist; results presented at local teaching and recommendations sent to Site Tutors for local inductions.

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: Poorer clerkings were linked to poor patient engagement and transfer from another ward. A survey of 8 trainees found no uniform method for capacity documentation and no official clerking checklist.
